name: Office of Future Plans
label: Dischord
lede: One opening slot in Baltimore, a cellist where a second guitarist would normally stand, and a band J. Robbins never meant to start that lasted seven years and made one album in his own studio.

eras.title: Never supposed to be a band
eras.text: By 2009 J. Robbins had fronted Jawbox, Burning Airlines and Channels, and was running his own Baltimore recording studio, the Magpie Cage. Office of Future Plans started as a favor: one opening slot for The Bomb, one pick-up band.

years.h: J. Robbins' son Callum is diagnosed with SMA
years.p: In 2007 J. Robbins' son Callum is diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy, an incurable nerve disorder, Wikipedia reports. Benefit shows are organized for the Robbins family in Chicago, Washington, Minneapolis and New York.

years.cap: Office of Future Plans · via Discogs
q: Office of Future Plans was never supposed to be a band.
years.h: Office of Future Plans starts as an opening slot for [[The Bomb|a056d886-5706-4a49-813d-ada40be71c93]]
years.p: J. Robbins is asked to open for Chicago punk band The Bomb in Baltimore and assembles [[Gordon Withers|5af1786c-c098-428c-9aec-261e3c9c5705]] on cello, [[Brooks Harlan|f9cb849f-568b-4987-b9cc-96e0e5d7d790]] on bass and his Channels drummer [[Darren Zentek|68c31f7f-f2e8-4353-92b7-c7ebf47f404d]], ex-[[Kerosene 454|3689eda0-1b6d-43f3-83ad-e58211ae7a3a]]. They keep going after the show.
years.xp:
Dischord's own history of the band opens with a disclaimer: it was meant to be a single gig. Instead the four kept writing, arranging and rehearsing at the Magpie Cage, and the label says the songs grew more collaborative and more layered as they went.

The line-up put a cello where a Jawbox fan would expect a second guitar, with Gordon Withers switching between cello and guitar.

eras.title: Made at the Magpie Cage
eras.text: Two years of rehearsals in J. Robbins' Magpie Cage studio turned into a single, then an album on Dischord, the label that had put out Jawbox's first records two decades earlier.

years.h: Office of Future Plans' first 7", 500 copies
years.p: Office of Future Plans self-release a two-song seven-inch in an edition of 500. Germany's Arctic Rodeo Recordings later repress it on colored vinyl.
The band's only album: twelve songs recorded at J. Robbins' Magpie Cage and mastered by Dan Coutant, from Salamander to Riddle Me This. Somewhere in the middle, a song called Fema Coffins.

years.h: "Lorelei" at the Rock and Roll Hotel, May 28, 2011
yt: "Lorelei" at the Rock and Roll Hotel, May 28, 2011

eras.title: A split, then the quiet end
eras.text: Office of Future Plans kept a lower profile after the album, putting out one more record, a split with Daria, before winding down. There was no farewell show on the record; the end came out in a Creative Loafing interview.

years.h: Office of Future Plans split a record with Daria
years.p: A split release by Office of Future Plans and the band Daria comes out on Lovitt Records, the D.C.-area label that had long worked with Dischord bands.

years.h: J. Robbins says Office of Future Plans is over
years.p: In an October 2016 interview with Creative Loafing, J. Robbins reveals that Office of Future Plans has broken up. Dischord lists the band's years as 2009–2016.

eras.title: Where the office went
eras.text: After Office of Future Plans, J. Robbins went solo and then back to Jawbox. Brooks Harlan went with him.

years.p: J. Robbins releases Un-Becoming, his first solo album.

years.h: J. Robbins' [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] back on the road
years.p: Jawbox, J. Robbins' band before Office of Future Plans, reunite for their first tour in more than twenty years.

When [[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]] leaves Jawbox, Brooks Harlan, J. Robbins' bandmate in Office of Future Plans and a guitarist in [[War on Women|69c05e9a-883b-4570-9c3d-c4bfc896a488]], takes his place.
years.xp: Barbot left citing the long commute from his new home in Vermont. Harlan, a longtime Robbins collaborator, stepped into the second-guitar spot, so a piece of Office of Future Plans now plays in Jawbox.
